title: Choose the visual world for MKE Budget Decoder
question: The roll assigned the Milwaukee sign-painter's window. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Sign-Painter's Window
options.lineage: Milwaukee corner-store window lettering, price boards, and Cream City brick ghost signs
options.thesis: Your city charges, lettered like a corner-store price board: the number is the sign.
options.viewport: Address typed into a lettered shop window; your 2027 total stands as the big price sign, 2026 small beside it, the line items a price board with a page tag on each.
options.risk: Hand lettering turns nostalgic or cute if overused; it must be reserved for numbers and headings, with a plain face for everything you read.

raised.raise: No boxes or cards: rank is carried by letter size alone, like a window where the price is the biggest thing.
One signature control: the Own / Rent switch re-letters the whole board in place, one pull, reversible.
Type is the material: no icons, illustrations, or gradients carry character; the lettering does.
One committed ground: the brick-cream field floods the screen instead of a white page with a colored card.
Selection steps forward: tapping a line lifts it to full size with its citation while the rest recede.

options.label: Blue Book Table
options.lineage: the Wisconsin Blue Book's statistical tables
options.thesis: The receipt as an almanac table: exact, dense, footnoted, trusted.
options.viewport: Address field over a two-column 2026 / 2027 table with a bold total row and numbered footnotes for every rate.
options.risk: Closest to the government-form feel you ruled out, and the familiar civic-data look most runs in this category land on.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Every charge arrives as lit digits; the 2026 to 2027 change is a visible roll of numerals.
options.viewport: Your 2027 total in a bank of glowing digits; each line item a smaller bank with an engraved label and page tag.
options.case: Wins on clarity, since the numbers are the interface and the change is literally visible; loses on audience, since a dark lab instrument doesn't read as Milwaukee civic life.
options.risk: Dark glow can read as gadget or fintech; contrast and motion need care for AA.

options.label: Cracktro Queue
options.thesis: Rank as depth on a black void, nothing boxed.
options.viewport: One ivory line of bitmap text over drifting dust.
options.case: Loses both: nobody in Milwaukee reads their city bill as a demo screen, and bitmap type hurts reading.
options.kept: No boxes or rules; rank carried by scale alone.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One pull turns a flat plane into shaped volume.
options.viewport: A black semicircle gathered by one gold cord.
options.case: Loses both: fashion couture has no link to a tax receipt.
options.risk: Luxury tone, the opposite of civic.
options.kept: One signature control that reshapes the whole surface.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.viewport: Words forming and breaking as weather fronts.
options.case: Loses both: moving letters fight exact numbers.

options.label: Yé-yé Sleeve
options.thesis: One flat saturated ground and a small ranked set.
options.viewport: Tangerine ground, four ranked titles in a corner.
options.case: Loses both: pop-record energy reads as marketing.
options.kept: Commit to one ground that floods the frame.

options.label: Console Atmosphere
options.thesis: Objects float in fog; selection swells forward.
options.viewport: Glowing cubes in a dark void.
options.case: Loses both: heavy 3D on a phone and no civic resonance.
options.kept: The selected item steps forward; the rest recede.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.viewport: Search bar, summary cards, then a table.
